Move the Outlook .ost file from drive C to drive D to free up space on drive C and optimize storage. 

1 - Backup All Data: Before starting, back up all Outlook data or the entire system to ensure safety in case of errors.

2 - Copy the .ost File to Drive D:
Close Outlook: Ensure Outlook is closed before copying the file. The .ost file cannot be copied while Outlook is open.
Copy the File: Navigate to the location of the .ost file (usually C:\Users\[YourUsername]\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook) and copy it to drive D.
*** Do Not Rename: Do not rename the file at this step; renaming should be done later in the process.

3 - Delete the Old Profile and Create a New Profile:
Delete Old Profile: Go to Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles and delete the old profile.
Create New Profile: In the same window, create a new profile. Select the manual setup option and specify the .ost file path to drive D.

4 - Delete the Newly Created .ost File:
Automatic Creation: The .ost file will be automatically created when you create a new profile.
Delete New File: After the new profile has been saved and configured, navigate to the location on drive D and delete this newly created .ost file.

5 - Rename the Copied .ost File:
Rename File: Rename the old .ost file (copied to drive D) to match the name of the new .ost file.

6 - Additional Notes:
Ensure that Outlook is configured correctly after the changes.
Verify that all email accounts and settings are working as expected.
Monitor the system for any issues related to the new .ost file location.

Solution for Power BI Data Not Updating
 
Issue: The data in Power BI is not updating because it is linked to an incorrect file.

Steps to Resolve:

Unlink and Reconnect Power BI to the Correct Excel File:
Open your Power BI Desktop file.
Go to the Home tab and click on Transform data.
Find the incorrect data source link and remove it.
Reconnect Power BI to the correct Excel file by selecting Get Data > Excel and navigating to the correct file.

Check and Fix Invalid Fields:
In the Query Editor, review the fields to ensure they are valid and correctly mapped.
Fix any fields that are not valid by updating the data types, renaming columns, or correcting any transformation steps.

Refresh the Connection:
After making the necessary corrections, go back to the Home tab in Power BI Desktop.
Click on Refresh to update the data connection and ensure the latest data is loaded.

Step-by-Step Guide to change the path of the ZaloPC folder from drive C to drive D using the mklink /j command:
Close ZaloPC:

Right-click on the Taskbar and select Task Manager.
In the Processes tab, find Zalo.
Right-click on Zalo and select End Task.
Move the ZaloPC Folder:

Navigate to C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\Local\ZaloPC (replace YourUsername with your actual username).
Cut the entire ZaloPC folder.
Paste it into D:\ZaloPC.
Create a Junction Link:

Open Command Prompt as an administrator:
Click the Start button, type cmd, right-click on Command Prompt, and select Run as administrator.
Enter the following command:
mklink /j "C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\Local\ZaloPC" "D:\ZaloPC"
Replace YourUsername with your actual username.
Verify the Link:

You should see a message saying "Junction created for C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\Local\ZaloPC <<===>> D:\ZaloPC".
Restart ZaloPC:

Open ZaloPC and ensure it runs correctly with the new folder path.
Additional Tips
Backup: It's a good idea to back up your ZaloPC data before making these changes.
Storage: Ensure that drive D has enough space to accommodate your ZaloPC data.

column31:
change the path of the ZaloPC folder from drive C to drive D using the mklink /j command to extend more space to his C drive

Step by step below:
Close ZaloPC:

Right-click on the Taskbar and select Task Manager.
In the Processes tab, find Zalo.
Right-click on Zalo and select End Task.
Move the ZaloPC Folder:

Navigate to C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\Local\ZaloPC (replace YourUsername with your actual username).
Cut the entire ZaloPC folder.
Paste it into D:\ZaloPC.
Create a Junction Link:

Open Command Prompt as an administrator:
Click the Start button, type cmd, right-click on Command Prompt, and select Run as administrator.
Enter the following command:
mklink /j "C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\Local\ZaloPC" "D:\ZaloPC"
Replace YourUsername with your actual username.
Verify the Link:

You should see a message saying "Junction created for C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\Local\ZaloPC <<===>> D:\ZaloPC".
Restart ZaloPC:

Open ZaloPC and ensure it runs correctly with the new folder path.
Additional Tips
Backup: It's a good idea to back up your ZaloPC data before making these changes.
Storage: Ensure that drive D has enough space to accommodate your ZaloPC data.

column31:
I checked and found that zalo count alot of storage:


Step-by-step guide to change the path of the ZaloPC folder from drive C to drive D using the mklink /j command:
Close ZaloPC:

Right-click on the Taskbar and select Task Manager.
In the Processes tab, find Zalo.
Right-click on Zalo and select End Task.
Move the ZaloPC Folder:

Navigate to C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\Local\ZaloPC (replace YourUsername with your actual username).
Cut the entire ZaloPC folder.
Paste it into D:\ZaloPC.
Create a Junction Link:

Open Command Prompt as an administrator:
Click the Start button, type cmd, right-click on Command Prompt, and select Run as administrator.
Enter the following command:
mklink /j "C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\Local\ZaloPC" "D:\ZaloPC"
Replace YourUsername with your actual username.
Verify the Link:

You should see a message saying "Junction created for C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\Local\ZaloPC <<===>> D:\ZaloPC".
Restart ZaloPC:

Open ZaloPC and ensure it runs correctly with the new folder path.
Additional Tips
Backup: It's a good idea to back up your ZaloPC data before making these changes.
Storage: Ensure that drive D has enough space to accommodate your ZaloPC data.

Helpdesk connected remotely to the user's laptop via TeamViewer (using the LSP-Guest wifi) and found that Cisco AnyConnect could not start. The following error was displayed: "Cisco AnyConnect failed to start. It is already running in another user's session."

This laptop is a shared device, and it is likely that another user had logged in previously and launched Cisco AnyConnect. When user spprt018 switched back to their session, Cisco was already running under a different user profile, which prevented it from starting again.

Solution:
Helpdesk explained the situation to the user and advised them to restart the laptop to terminate all existing user sessions. After rebooting, user spprt018 was able to open Cisco AnyConnect and connect to wifi LSPConnect successfully.

Helpdesk has also:
Run "Disk Clean Up" with Admin permission to clean up Windows update log files & temp files.
Checked and see that the Zalo Data files account for 28.6GB - which is currently in Disk C -> HD moved this Zalo Data files to Disk D by going to Zalo Settings -> Data Management -> Click the "Move" button to move data to Disk D.

column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Issue Summary:
 User encountered an error when launching zalo.exe from the Desktop with the following message:
 Windows cannot access the specified device, path, or file. You may not have the appropriate permissions to access the item.
Root Cause:
 The issue was caused by Windows Defender’s Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rule:
 “Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criteria.”
 This rule flagged zalo.exe (located on the user's Desktop) as suspicious, even though it is a legitimate application. The file was blocked due to one or more of the following reasons:
It was not launched from a trusted location.
It may not meet Microsoft's prevalence or trust criteria (e.g., new, uncommon hash).
It was executed via explorer.exe, which was the process flagged in the ASR block.
Resolution Steps:
Verified the source of the blocked file and confirmed it matches the legitimate Zalo installation in:
 C:\Users\nhulta\AppData\Local\Programs\Zalo\zalo.exe.
Removed the manually copied zalo.exe from Desktop.
Created a proper shortcut to the original zalo.exe in the Zalo installation directory.
Tested the shortcut – application launched successfully with no ASR block.
Current Status:
 Issue resolved. User is now able to open Zalo via the desktop shortcut without security intervention.
Recommendation:
 For future use, avoid placing executable files directly on the Desktop. Instead, use shortcuts pointing to the application's original location. This reduces the likelihood of ASR false positives.

Step-by-step IT resolution guide, Issue Summary: Chaloempan cannot log into their SCG domain account. Error:"Sign-in failed. The KDC certificate could not be validated."

Resolution Steps

Step 1:
1. At the login screen where the error appears: Turn off Wi-Fi using the Wi-Fi icon on the bottom right.
2. Log in again using the same domain username and password. Windows should now use cached credentials.
Login should succeed, as he has logged in before on this device.

Step 2: Reconnect to the SCG Network
1. After successful login:
Turn Wi-Fi back on.
Connect to an available internet network (e.g., home Wi-Fi).
Launch VPN Cisco AnyConnect.
2. Verify VPN connection is successful.

Step 3: Re-Authenticate with Domain Controller
1. Once VPN is connected, Press Windows + L to lock the screen and let them log in again using their SCG domain credentials.

2. This time, authentication will go through VPN → SCG Domain Controller. The KDC certificate will be validated.
Windows domain services (Kerberos, Group Policy, SSO) will sync correctly.

Step 4 Check again: turn off vpn, reconnect to LSPConnect wifi and lock the screen again then let him unlock -> now can unlock normally without turning off the wifi like step 1.

column2: [LSP Printer] - Printer is not showing the print job
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Issue Summary: The user (Ms. Hằng) reported that she was unable to print documents via the network printer connected through the Print Server (LSPPrinter). However, when IT support arrived to check the issue, everything was working normally and printing succeeded without any errors.

Root Cause Analysis: In the morning, Ms. Hằng could not connect to the company network, so she temporarily used her phone's 4G hotspot to continue working.

It is likely that during the time she attempted to print, her laptop was still connected to the 4G network instead of the internal Wi-Fi (LSPConnect).

Since the printer server only works over the internal network, the printing failed while on 4G.

IT Resolution (Point by Point):

1. Initial Report: User unable to print via network printer (LSPPrinter).

2. On-Site Check: IT support verified printer and network – all functions normal.

3. Observation: Device was connected to internal Wi-Fi (LSPConnect) during the support session.

4. User Behavior Identified: The User had earlier switched to 4G hotspot due to network issues.

5. Likely Scenario: Printing attempt was made while connected to 4G, not the internal network.

6. Conclusion: The issue was caused by user being on the wrong network (not internal Wi-Fi).


7. Resolution: Advised user to always reconnect to internal Wi-Fi before using internal services like printing.


8. Action Taken: No system fault found; resolved as user behavior case.

Case Summary: LSPConnect Not Connecting on First Login (New User Mr. An)

User: Mr. An (newcomer)
PC: DVT-MTN-04
Issue Reported: On first login, Wi-Fi LSPConnect stayed in the “Connecting” state, and Cisco AnyConnect showed “Limited or No Connectivity”.
Purpose of AnyConnect for posture validation via Cisco ISE.

This was Mr. An’s first login ever on this PC. At that time: Cisco AnyConnect could not yet validate his posture through ISE. The system remained stuck at "Connecting", and Cisco AnyConnect showed "Limited or No Connectivity".

Troubleshooting Actions Taken

1. Logged into the same PC with Ms Thuy's account (a known working user):
LSPConnect connected normally.
Cisco AnyConnect status showed "Compliant".
This proved that the PC configuration, Wi-Fi adapter, and ISE policies were working as expected.
2. From Ms Thuy's session:
Exited Cisco AnyConnect manually.
Locked screen (Win + L), then allowed Mr. An to log in.
Wi-Fi remained connected (session still active).
Cisco AnyConnect was launched under Mr. An’s session → this time, posture validation passed, and status: "Compliant".
3. The PC was shut down and restarted.
Mr. An logged in directly.
LSPConnect connected successfully.
Cisco AnyConnect posture status: "Compliant" → confirmed OK.

Error Message:
When executing the flow LSPMealOrder-NewOrder.Run from PowerApps, the following error occurs:"User with id ... does not have ReadAccess right(s) for record ... of entity Process."

Root Cause:
The user does not have Read access to a record in the Process (or Workflow) entity in Dynamics 365, where flow definitions are stored.
Context:
The app works fine in the developer's environment.
Even though the user has the same license and app permissions, the flow fails when triggered.
The developer assumed the flow would run using a preset connection (i.e., the flow owner's connection), but instead, it tries to run under the app user's context, which lacks permission.
Actions Taken:
✅ Verified that the user has access to the app and the 4 SharePoint lists used
✅ Conductlive monitoring session with the user to inspect the issue in real-time.
✅ Share access to user on Flow => User now can use app in normal

System Status Check: Laptop was found to be in a pending update state, which can affect performance.

Update Process: A full restart was performed to apply all pending updates.

Uptime Review: The laptop had been running continuously for 4 days and 23 hours without a shutdown.
A proper shutdown was executed to refresh system resources and improve performance.

Post-Restart Status: After restarting and completing updates, the laptop is now operating normally.

Root Cause 

The laptop was experiencing slow performance due to the following factors:

Pending System Updates: The system was in a "pending update" state, which can consume background resources and degrade performance until updates are applied.

Extended Uptime Without Restart: The laptop had been running continuously for nearly 5 days without a proper shutdown or restart.
This prolonged uptime can lead to memory leaks, background process buildup, and reduced system responsiveness.

Error: Your computer's Trusted Platform Module has malfunctioned. If this error persists, contact your system administrator with error code C0090016.


Solution:
I identified that the issue was related to a conflict with theTrusted Platform Module (TPM)on the device, causing sign-in failures for Microsoft applications such asOutlook, OneDrive, and Teams.
I proceeded toreset the TPMby following these steps (as refered by Microsoft:https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/troubleshoot/activation/tpm-malfunctioned)
Settings → Privacy & security → Windows security → Device Security → Security processor → Security processor details → Clear TPM
After restarting the device and signing back intoOutlook, OneDrive, and Microsoft Teams, all services functioned normally again.

IT Resolution: [LSP Laptop] - My Laptop Screen is Dark
 
Issue Summary:
User reported that the laptop screen brightness was unusually low, making it difficult to view content clearly.

Root Cause:
The laptop was operating in a power-saving mode, which automatically reduces screen brightness to conserve battery life. This behavior is typical in Windows when the Power Mode is set to "Balanced" or "Power Saver."

Resolution Steps:
Navigated to Settings > System > Power & Battery.
Verified that the Power Mode was set to a lower performance setting.
Changed the Power Mode to​ Best Performance for both "Plugged in" and "On battery" scenarios.
Screen brightness immediately increased to normal levels.


Result: The screen brightness issue was resolved. The laptop now displays at full brightness, improving visibility and user experience.

Issue: With PDF X-change editor still slow little bit
Because: PDF-XChange Editor can print more slowly than other viewers for several main reasons: its rendering engine handles complex elements (graphics, transparency, fonts) differently; some printing configurations still use GDI instead of XPS/DirectX, which is less efficient; the “Print as Image” option, when enabled, converts pages to images and is very time-consuming; PDFs with many layers, high-resolution images, or annotations require longer pre-processing; incompatible or faulty printer drivers can also slow printing; and because PDF-XChange Editor is feature-rich and heavier than lightweight viewers like Edge, it may take longer to send print jobs.
Result: If user want to print smoothly, user can use another PDF like: Adobe Acrobat, PDF Gear.

1. Log in to the Security Info Portal:

Sign in with your SCG/LSP account credentials.



2. Add a New Sign-In Method:

On the Security info page, select + Add sign-in method.

From the list, choose Authenticator app, then click Add.



3. Set Up Microsoft Authenticator:

On your phone, open the Microsoft Authenticator app.

Select Add account → Work or school account → Scan QR code.

On your computer, select Next in the setup wizard until the QR code appears.

Use your phone to scan the QR code.



4. Complete Verification:

After scanning, the app will display your account in the list.

On your computer, click Next and approve the test notification sent to your mobile device.



5. Confirm and Save:

The new Authenticator method will now appear in your Security info list.

Keep both MFA methods active for backup purposes.

Result: Windows temporarily considers the file as non-existent/inaccessible.

3. Resolution

1. Restart the computer (do not use Shut down).
  
2.  After restarting, Windows completes replacing the file, Zalo runs normally again.

Remind the user to Restart immediately when Windows indicates that a restart is required to complete the update.

column31:
Solution Summary

Performed a hard shutdown (connected charger → hold power button to force shutdown → restart).
After the restart, the Wi-Fi adapter was recognized and was working normally again.

Remoted and Checked Event Viewer logs and identified Wi-Fi adapter errors:(24 Aug 2025 -the day before error)
“Intel(R) Wi-Fi 6 AX201 160MHz: Has determined that the network adapter is not functioning properly.”
“Intel(R) Wi-Fi 6 AX201 160MHz: Has encountered an internal error and has failed.”



Applied all pending Windows Updates (including drivers and patches).
Monitoring user activity for the rest of the day to confirm stability.

---

Root Cause Explanation

The Wi-Fi adapter encountered an internal driver/firmware error and stopped responding. A regular restart may not fully reset the device. By performing a hard shutdown, the system completely cut off power to the adapter, forcing it to reset both hardware and driver state. Upon reboot, the adapter reloaded its firmware and resumed normal functionality.

column2: [Excel Issue] - Can not save file - some things change in the Options setting
column12: P4 (This represents a minor issue and a simple request that only impacts an individual)
column31:
IT Resolution: Reset Excel to Default Settings

Issue
User reports that Excel displays the error:
> “Excel ran out of resources while attempting to calculate one or more formulas.”
This happened after Ms Van changes were made to Excel Formula Options (e.g., iterative calculation, calculation mode).

Root Cause
Non-default Formulas settings (Manual calculation, Iterative calculation enabled).
Potential circular references leading to infinite recalculation.
Large formulas stressing Excel’s memory resources.

Resolution Steps
​
Option 1 – Restore Formula Settings to Default (Recommended first step)
1. Open Excel → File → Options → Formulas.
2. Configure back to defaults:
Workbook Calculation: Automatic
Uncheck: Enable iterative calculation
Maximum Iterations: 100 (default)
Maximum Change: 0.001 (default)
3. Click OK, restart Excel, and retest.

Option 2 – Office Repair (Full Reset)
1. Open Control Panel → Programs and Features.
2. Select Microsoft Office → Change → choose:
Quick Repair (fast, keeps most data)
or Online Repair (complete reset, requires internet).
3. Reboot PC, relaunch Excel.

The company uses a synchronized account system where AD credentials and Microsoft 365 accounts are unified.

Informed the user that they must always log into their workstation with the latest AD/Microsoft 365 password after a reset or change.

Assisted the user in signing out and logging back into Windows with the updated credentials.

Verified that the user could successfully access the file server after using the new password.

Step 1: Right-click the Teams icon in the system tray (bottom-right corner of the screen) → select Quit.

Open File Explorer.

Step 2: Paste the following path into the address bar and press Enter:
%appdata%\Microsoft\Teams


Step 3: Delete all the folders and files inside (especially: Cache, blob_storage, databases, GPUCache, IndexedDB, Local Storage, tmp).
Restart Teams → sign in again.

Result: After clear cache. User can send text in MS Teams normally

Lenovo L14 Gen 2 laptops slow/lag during normal use.

Root Cause
Cumulative Update (KB5056431) installed first → consumed high CPU, RAM, and Disk I/O.
After that, Windows detected many driver & security pending updates.
While these were downloading/installing, system resources were heavily used → causing lag.

Resolution
Allow Windows to complete all pending updates and perform necessary restarts.  
Once updates finish, Windows Update services and installer processes stop consuming resources.

System returns to normal performance because:
No more heavy background install tasks.
Drivers and cumulative patches are stabilized.

column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Cause:
Extended Uptime: The machine's uptime is currently exceeding 7 days, which often leads to accumulated resource conflicts and stale security tokens.
Credential Conflict: M365 applications often try to use saved Windows credentials. If the Windows password has expired, or if the system lags when retrieving credentials from the Credential Manager, the application will send invalid credentials to the Proxy server and be denied access.
Resolution: Perform a System Reboot
Cache Reset: It clears all expired tokens and corrupted DNS/Proxy cache entries in system memory.
Service Restart: It ensures that the Windows Proxy and Network services restart cleanly, allowing them to request the latest credentials from the user or the Credential Manager.
Credential Refresh: Logging back into Windows refreshes the user's credentials, thereby fixing the temporary storage problem within the Credential Manager.

column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Issue Summary: 
The problem occurred because the user had saved old credentials when connecting to internal resources (such as printer servers or file servers). The “Remember my credentials” option caused Windows to keep using outdated login information even after the user changed their password.


Root Cause:
The user selected “Remember my credentials”, which stored the old username and password in Windows Credential Manager. After the password was updated, the system still tried to authenticate using the saved (now invalid) credentials, resulting in an access error.


Resolution:
Instruct users not to select “Remember my credentials” when connecting to internal servers or shared folders.
Explain that this option saves their old password, which can cause login failures after a password change.
If users have already saved old credentials, guide them to remove them from Credential Manager (Control Panel → Credential Manager → Windows Credentials → Remove or Edit).
After removing, reconnect to the resource and re-enter the updated username and password.

User Explanation (simplified): “When you tick ‘Remember my credentials,’ Windows keeps your old password saved. After you change your password, it still tries to log in with the old one — that’s why you get an error. Next time, don’t tick that box; just enter your new password when asked.”

On 13 October 2025, Mr. Eaknarin Huangnum changed his Active Directory password. To ensure continued access across all devices, he needs to update the new password accordingly:

WiFi LSPConnect – Update the password on his laptop.
WiFi LSPInternet – Update the password on his mobile devices.
Support was provided to help him forget the old WiFi settings and reconnect using the new password on all relevant devices.

IT Resolution – Screen Flickering Issue

User Report:
User reported intermittent screen flickering and display instability on their laptop.


Investigation Findings:
Pending Windows Updates Identified
Multiple Intel and Dell driver updates were found pending in Windows Update.
These include critical updates related to display, system components, and firmware.
Key Drivers Potentially Causing Flickering:
Intel Graphics Driver (32.0.101.6881) 
Controls screen rendering; outdated versions may cause flickering or instability.
Confirmed as a critical update by Dell (dated 12 Aug 2025).
Intel System/SoftwareComponent Packages 
Interface with GPU and chipset; mismatched versions may affect display timing.
Dell Firmware Updates 
May impact display initialization and power delivery.
Realtek Audio Drivers 
Low risk, but may affect HDMI/DisplayPort handshakes.


Root Cause Hypothesis:
The flickering is most likely caused by the pending Intel Graphics Driver update, which includes bug fixes and stability improvements for Iris Xe GPUs.


Resolution Steps:
Completed all pending Windows and Dell updates, especially the Intel Graphics Driver.
Performed a system reboot after updates were installed.
Rechecked display behavior to confirm resolution of flickering issue.

Move ZaloData Folder to Drive D
Step 1: Close Zalo completely.

Step 2: Copy the folder ZaloData from
C:\Users\%username%\AppData\Roaming\ZaloData
to a new location on drive D, for example:
D:\%username%-zalodata\ZaloData

Step 3: Delete or rename the original ZaloData folder in the C drive.
Step 4: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run the following command:
mklink /j "C:\Users\%username%\AppData\Roaming\ZaloData" "D:\%username%-zalodata\ZaloData"
This creates a symbolic link so Zalo still accesses the data as if it were in the original location.
Step 5: Open Zalo and check if it works normally.
Step 6: Once confirmed, you can delete the old ZaloData folder from the C drive (if not already done).

column2: Unable to Open Camera When Selecting “Photo” Option in J5
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
1. Root Cause 
Application Misidentification: The initial fault was not due to the J5 Mobile application itself or the "Open Camera" application; instead, the J5 application was actually calling the system's Default Camera Application when the user pressed the "Photo/Video" button.
Missing Configuration: The faulty ISafe devices (IS-DWM-00x) were either missing or had the necessary Default Camera Application disabled (uninstalled/deactivated), and they lacked the required access permissions for J5 to successfully call the function.

2. Resolution Process
Diagnosis: After conducting cross-checks and determining the fault was not with the J5 software or the ISAFE device model in general, IT confirmed the root cause was the missing Default Camera application.
Test Attempt 1 (Integration Fix): IT deployed the default camera installation package (org.codeaurora.snapcam) from a known working test machine to the user's devices.
Result of Test 1: This fixed the integration (J5 could successfully call the Camera function), but the newly deployed camera application immediately crashed.
Final Fix: IT continued a deeper investigation and successfully identified and deployed a different, stable alternative camera application.

3. Final Outcome
The issue has been fully resolved by deploying a compatible and stable alternative camera application.
The J5 Mobile application can now successfully call the photo/video functionality without crashing on all six of the user's devices (IS-DWM-001 to IS-DWM-006).

column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Cause:
The application AMS Machinery Manager had previously worked on the device DVT-PHUCNHO, but after a Windows update, new inbound rules were created and automatically set to Deny.
During installation, the system generates two inbound rules (MtDbMgr and NetAdmin). If the installation is not performed using the itsupport admin account, these rules are created in Deny mode, preventing the application from functioning.
The application also requires a vendor-provided registration code linked to the assigned serial number, which the user could not complete on their own.
Solution:
Reinstalled AMS Machinery Manager on device DVT-PHUCNHO.
Ensured the installation was executed using the itsupport admin account so that the required inbound rules (MtDbMgr and NetAdmin) were created correctly.
Manually reviewed and adjusted the firewall rules, changing both rules from Deny to Allow to enable proper communication.
Coordinated with the vendor to obtain the required registration code, as AMS applications must be activated by the vendor using the device’s assigned serial number.
Completed the activation and confirmed successful registration.
Result:
AMS Machinery Manager was fully installed, activated, and functioning normally on DVT-PHUCNHO.
All firewall rules were correctly configured, and the user can now use the software without restrictions.

column2: [Windows Update] - Laptop Shows Notification About Missing Updates
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Issue:
Laptop joined to theSCG (Thailand) domain → receives theSCG domain WSUS.
Now used in theLSP network, where SCG WSUS is unreachable.
Result: Windows shows “You’re up to date” but still missing security updates (forced bySCGWSUS )
Root Cause:
This forces updates only from SCG WSUS — even when offline from it -SCG network
Windows Update Agent (WUA) doesn’t contact Microsoft Update directly → false “up to date” status.
Why “Check online from Microsoft Update” Works:
Temporarily bypasses WSUS policy (ignores UseWUServer=1).
Contacts Microsoft update endpoints directly (e.g., https://fe2.update.microsoft.com).
Retrieves full update catalog → installs missing updates successfully.
Microsoft Explanation:
“If a device is configured to receive updates from WSUS, Windows Update will not contact Microsoft Update directly unless the user chooses to check online.”

mklink /j "C:\Users\%username%\AppData\Roaming\ZaloData" "D:\ZaloData"

 Step 6: After confirming, you can delete the old ZaloData folder from drive C (if not already removed).

column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Resolution Summary 

Actions Taken:
Identified the faulty print job of user khanhngd in the printer queue on the Print Server (\\LSPSRVPRDPRT\OILSP_PRINTER).
Canceled and deleted the stuck print job (Job ID: 29998).


Result:
Printing function returned to normal operation.
Other users were able to print without any issue.
No need to restart the Print Spooler service or the printer device.

Technical Explanation:
When a print job encounters an Error – In Queue state, the Windows Print Spooler Service retains a reference to that job in the spool files, typically located at C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS.
The system does not automatically clear the queue in order to prevent loss of pending print data.
The corrupted job remains locked in the queue, occupying the first position and blocking subsequent jobs from the same user, though other users remain unaffected (different sessions or permission contexts).
By canceling the faulty job, the spooler removes the related.SPL and SHD files, releasing the queue and allowing subsequent jobs to process normally.

column2: [Win 11 Update] - Support Request – Windows 11 Update Issue
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Reason / Rationale 
Laptop fail to install feature updates of Windows 11 because the small “System Reserved” or “EFI System” partition (often ~100 MB) is too full or too small to accommodate update operations.
The update process (for example servicing of the Windows Recovery Environment or boot-components) requires extra free space in that partition. Microsoft’s documentation reports the error: “We couldn’t update the system reserved partition” when the partition is full.

To fix it either you free space inside that partition, or enlarge it (for example by adding ~200 MB). The Microsoft article KB5028997 gives “Instructions to manually resize your partition …” for WinRE updates.
Windows Update Fix – System Reserved Partition Full



Fix Windows 11 feature updates (e.g., 25H2) by expanding the EFI/System Reserved partition.

1. Boot into WinPE
Use a Windows PE or any bootable partition tool (e.g., MiniTool Partition Wizard Bootable).

2. Launch Partition Tool
Open Partition Wizard (or similar).

3. Identify the EFI/System Reserved Partition
Usually:
Label: EFI System Partition / System Reserved
Size: ~100 MB
Format: FAT32 (UEFI) or NTFS (Legacy BIOS)
Type: System or Boot

4. Shrink Adjacent Partition (Usually C:): Reduce C: by 200 MB (from the left side).
This creates unallocated space next to the EFI partition.

5. Extend EFI/System Reserved Partition: Select the EFI/SRP → Extend → Add 200 MB from the unallocated space.
Apply the change.

6. Apply and Reboot: Confirm all operations → reboot into normal Windows.

7. Verify in Disk Management: EFI/SRP should now be around 300 MB+ total.

8. Run Windows Update Again
Open Settings → Windows Update → Check for updates.
The 25H2 update should now install successfully.

IssueL: Some messages from sender Huyen Dang Thi Diu (huyentd@lsp.com) were automatically moved from the Inbox to the “Read mail” folder, including unread emails. 
---

Root Cause: Outlook Web’s Sweep feature had an active rule under
Settings → Mail → Sweep → “Messages from Huyen Dang Thi Diu”.

The rule was set to “Move all messages from the Read mail folder”, which automatically moved both read and unread messages out of the Inbox once they matched the condition.

Sweep rules run automatically and periodically on the mailbox until manually disabled or deleted.
Microsoft reference: Microsoft Learn – Organize your Inbox using Sweep rules in Outlook.com

Resolution Steps Performed
1. Opened Outlook Web App → Settings (⚙️) → View all Outlook settings → Mail → Sweep.
2. Identified the active Sweep rule: Messages from Huyen Dang Thi Diu → Enabled.
3. Switched the toggle OFF to disable the rule (or optionally deleted the rule).
  4. Verified Inbox: all messages, including unread ones, stopped being auto-moved and stayed in the Inbox.

After disabling the rule, Outlook no longer performs automatic “Sweep” actions on new or existing messages from this sender.

Issue: User unable to print to the network printer server (10.45.8.25). Print queue was empty, suggesting an initial connection/authentication failure.

Root Cause Analysis
The issue was a mismatch between the current user password and the stored Windows Credentials.
Authentication Requirement: Printing to a shared network resource (printer) requires the client machine to successfully authenticate against the server (10.45.8.25).
Mismatched Credentials: The user's account (witadath) password was changed on 10/2/2025

The stored Windows Credential for 10.45.8.25 was last modified on 27/08/2025 

=> Failure Mechanism (MCSA Principle): The client attempted to authenticate using the outdated (pre-10/2/2025) password stored in the Credential Manager. The server rejected the session due to invalid credentials, blocking the print job from entering the queue.
Resolution (Point-to-Point)
Action: The outdated credential entry for 10.45.8.25 was located in the user's Windows Credential Manager.
Execution: This entry was removed/updated to reflect the current password.
Outcome: Authentication succeeded, and the user was immediately able to print documents.
When logging LSP AD account to connect to \\10.45.8.25 to connect printer, please don't tick Remember account

Issue Description
Error Message:
“The code execution cannot proceed because CTL3D32.dll was not found. Reinstalling the program may fix this problem.”
Affected Application:vnpt-ca_ace_certd.exe(VNPT Token software)
Root Cause:Missing or corruptedCTL3D32.dllfile, which is a required dynamic link library for the VNPT Token application.

Resolution Steps
1. Verify the Error
Confirm that the error appears when launching the VNPT Token application.


2. Identify the Requirement
The VNPT Token software requires certain DLL files to function correctly.
Missing DLL files typically occur due to:
Incomplete installation
Corrupted files
Manual deletion or antivirus interference

3. Apply the Recommended Fix
The error message suggests:“Reinstalling the program may fix this problem.”
Therefore, proceed withreinstallation of the VNPT Token software.

4. Reinstall VNPT Token
Steps:
Plug in the USB VNPT Token
Uninstall the existing VNPT Token software from the laptop
Restart the laptop (to clear any locked files).
Install the VNPT Token software againfrom the USB folder
Ensure installation completes without errors.

5. Validate the Fix
Launch the VNPT Token application after reinstallation.
Confirm that the error no longer appears and the application runs normally.
Check if the required DLL (CTL3D32.dll) is now present in the application directory.

Final Outcome
Resolution:Reinstalling the VNPT Token software restored the missing DLL file and resolved the error.
Status:Issue fixed successfully.

Cause:
The Ricoh C3500 printer displayed an authentication error (Error Code: S0409-000), preventing users from printing or scanning.

Solution:
Verified account validity by testing login with a different user ID and credentials.
After confirming the issue originated from the printer, performed the following steps:
Powered off the printer, waited 3 minutes, and powered it back on.
When the issue persisted, unplugged and reconnected the LAN cable at the back of the printer.
The printer regained network connection immediately after the LAN cable was reseated.

Result:
The Ricoh C3500 returned to normal operation, with users able to authenticate and print successfully.
The root cause was determined to be a loose LAN cable, causing temporary loss of connection to the print server.

column2: Trouble with GC software
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Regarding the user's ticket request:
The user reported an error related to the Agilent ChemStation software (GC DHA Data Analysis Module) that appears after the completion of each sample test. The system displayed error dialogs stating: "ChemSpool Information: Print Spooler is not responding" and "System resources are low".
1. Root Cause Analysis
Based on the inspection of the Task Manager and Temp folder, the error is identified as a Process Conflict and Print Buffer Overflow:

Stuck Processes: The Task Manager showed at least three parallel instances of "ChemStation ChemMain (32 bit)" running.
Reason: The software may have hung in previous sessions without exiting completely, or the user accidentally opened it multiple times.

Consequence: These processes compete for resources and conflict over device control.
Temp File Locking: The folder C:\Users\GC-DHA\AppData\Local\Temp contains many continuously created .tmp files (e.g., P3D36A5.tmp, JOB9604.tmp).
Reason: When printing reports, ChemStation creates temporary files. With multiple ChemStation instances running simultaneously, they attempt to access or overwrite the same temp files or system page files, causing the "has problems with page file" error.

The black-screen issue on the laptop was caused by a corrupted or incompatible Intel graphics driver, not by hardware damage. The system was still running in the background (backlight on, keyboard responding), which matches Microsoft’s documented behavior when the display driver fails to load. 

After updating all required Intel and system drivers through Windows Update — especially the Intel Graphics, Chipset, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and Realtek Audio drivers — the display pipeline (WDDM) was restored to a stable state.
As a result, the laptop returned to normal operation with no visual abnormalities.

This confirms that:
The screen panel and internal cables were not faulty.
The issue was fully resolved by installing the correct drivers.

The solution aligns with Microsoft and Intel’s official guidelines for black-screen symptoms caused by driver failure.
Trusted Microsoft & Intel References
1. Microsoft – Troubleshooting Black Screen Issues
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/troubleshoot/windows-black-screen

column2: [LSP Laptop] - The display on my laptop keeps flickering
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Incident: Screen Flickering on Lenovo Laptop
Device info (from CMD screenshot):
Hostname: LVT-ANHTN
BIOS SerialNumber: PF3NYJDO
Symptoms
Intermittent screen flickering observed on Windows 11.
Flicker occurs during normal desktop use and while Windows Update/Vantage are active.
Initial Assessment (Before Updates)
Windows Update showed multiple pending driver updates: 
Intel Corporation – Display 32.0.101.6881 (downloading)
Intel Corporation – Extension 32.0.101.6881
Intel – SoftwareComponent 25.91.103.0 / 25.12.7.3.0
Lenovo – System 10.2.2.6
Lenovo – Firmware 1.19.0
Intel – net 23.150.0.4
SAMSUNG Electronics – USB 2.21.0.0
Actions Taken
Windows Update
Completed available updates, including Intel graphics stack (Display + Extensions + SoftwareComponent), Lenovo System, Realtek, and Samsung USB packages.
From the second screenshot, additional update wave included: 
Intel Corporation Driver Update (Display) 32.0.101.7077
Intel Corporation Driver Update (Display) 32.0.101.7026 (another bundle pass)
Lenovo – System 10.15.2509.1
Realtek Driver Update 1153.19.603.2025
Windows Defender intelligence and KB5027066 (.NET 8)
Lenovo Vantage / System Update
Ran Lenovo System Update to align vendor firmware/components.
Confirmed Synaptics Touchpad Firmware Update Tool applied (progress reached 92% in screenshot), and Lenovo Firmware/System packages were completed.
Reboot
Per Windows Update prompt (“Restart required – estimate 2 min”), performed system restart to finalize driver/firmware installations.
Root Cause (Technical)
Outdated Intel Graphics driver caused panel timing instability with Windows 11’s desktop compositor (DWM).
The flicker is consistent with issues arising from Intel graphics driver builds prior to 32.0.101.702x/7077, where Panel Self Refresh (PSR) and refresh‑rate negotiation on embedded DisplayPort (eDP) panels may intermittently glitch during mode switches, brightness changes, or overlay composition.
Resolution
Primary Fix: Updating the Intel Graphics (Display) driver to a current build eliminated the flicker.
Resolved by: Intel Corporation – Display 32.0.101.7077 (installed via Windows Update).
Supporting components also updated: Intel Corporation – Extension 32.0.101.7026/7077, Intel SoftwareComponent 25.91.103.0, and Lenovo System/Firmware packages, ensuring full stack consistency.
Post‑update result: No screen flickering observed after reboot and sustained monitoring during normal use. Display stable under idle and load.

IT Resolution Summary
Issue:
Laptop fails to resume from sleep/hibernate → forced cold boot.
Root Cause
Primary: HAL Error (Event ID 21) – ACPI Timer/Alarm Device failed, preventing RTC configuration.
Contributing: Pending driver and firmware updates (Intel, Realtek, Dell) caused instability in power state transitions.
Multiple Intel, Realtek, and Dell updates were listed as “Downloading” or “Pending install.” Unfinished driver installations (especially firmware/system components) frequently cause power state management instability and conflicts with the ACPI framework.







Evidence
Event ID 6008: Unexpected shutdown → confirms hard crash.
Event ID 21: ACPI evaluation failure → HAL-level power management issue.
Windows Update: Multiple critical updates pending (drivers/firmware).
Resolution Steps
Install All Pending Updates: 
Go to Settings > Windows Update → Complete all downloads and installs.
Restart the system after updates.

Which Updates Directly Affect the Keyboard?
The keyboard functionality is typically controlled by:
Intel Chipset Drivers (System Components)
Updates labeled Intel Corporation – System and Intel Corporation – Extension are critical because they include chipset and input device drivers that manage keyboard communication with the motherboard.
Firmware Updates (Dell Inc. – Firmware)
Firmware updates can fix hardware-level issues, including keyboard responsiveness.
Optional: HID (Human Interface Device) Drivers
These are usually bundled under System or Input Device updates.

Most Relevant Packages for Keyboard
Intel Corporation – System
Intel Corporation – Extension
Dell Inc. – Firmware
These updates ensure proper functioning of the keyboard by updating chipset drivers and firmware that control input devices.

column31:
Resolution
The screen flickering issue on the Dell Latitude 3440 is primarily due to outdated graphics drivers and an incomplete BIOS update. Images confirm pending driver updates (Intel, Realtek) and a BIOS update in progress (from v1.24.0 to v1.26.0).
Root Cause:
Outdated or corrupt Intel graphics drivers.
Intel(R) Corporation - Extension - 1.0.3832.0 
Intel - net - 23.110.0.5
Intel Corporation - Bluetooth - 23.100.11
Intel Corporation - Extension - 32.0.101.6556 (strong candidate for graphics driver update)
Intel - SoftwareComponent - 1.46.2024.221
Intel - SoftwareComponent - 1.7.4.230.0
Pending BIOS update causing system instability.




Recommended Fix:
Follow a two-phase update process:
Complete BIOS Update
Restart the system to finalize the BIOS upgrade to v1.26.0.
Verify the update after reboot.
Install All Pending Drivers
Use Windows Update to install Intel, Realtek, and Dell drivers.
Perform a final restart after installation.
Key Notes:
Keep the laptop connected to AC power during updates.
Do not interrupt the BIOS flashing process.
Intel Extension and SoftwareComponent updates likely include graphics driver fixes.

Terminates the broken MFA authentication session
Forces a new, clean sign-in flow
Generates a fresh session key correctly bound to the Long Son tenant

column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Why .POTX can’t be edited in the browser
.pptx = presentation document → meant to be edited as a normal slide deck.
.potx = template file → meant to be used to create new presentations, not to be edited directly like a deck.
In SharePoint / OneDrive / PowerPoint for the web, Microsoft commonly treats template formats (like .potx) as “create from template / download and open” rather than “edit in browser”.
So the online editor may show no Edit option or it opens in a restricted way because the platform expects you to generate a .pptx from the template first.

column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Resolution:
The issue was caused by the laptop running continuously for 10 days without a full shutdown.


Due to Windows' long uptime, the Cisco Secure Client Posture service did not refresh its status correctly.As a result, Cisco ISE could not retrieve the correct posture and OS information, and the device was temporarily identified with an incorrect endpoint profile.
On Cisco ISE (time of error)
Authentication SUCCESSFUL (5200) → 802.1X does not fail
Endpoint Profile: Windows8-Workstation (incorrect)
Authorization Result:
LSP_Posture_Remediation_Unknown
Posture Status: Pending / Unknown
Meaning: Authentication OK, but posture and profile are incorrect → placed in restricted VLAN
=> The system was therefore placed into a restricted network state, resulting in “Connected but No Internet”.
  
  
The system was therefore placed into a restricted network state, resulting in “Connected but No Internet”.
A full shutdown and restart reset the operating system, network stack, and posture services.

After reboot, the posture check completed successfully, the correct Windows 11 endpoint profile was applied, and normal network access was restored.

Posture restarts normally
Endpoint Profile: Windows11-Workstation
Authorization Result: LSP_Posture_Compliant
Received normal IP → Wi-Fi has Internet
802.11 association successful
802.1X EAP-TLS Authentication succeeded (5200) → Excludes RF, Wi-Fi driver, and credential.

Resolution
The issue occurs because the meeting organizer tried to book a recurring meeting beyond the allowed booking window for the meeting room. The system declined the request because the booking window limit is set to 730 days (2 years) in the Exchange Admin Center.

How to Check the Limited Days for Scheduling a Meeting Room
Step 1: Access Exchange Admin Center
Open your browser and go to:
https://admin.exchange.microsoft.com
Log in with your admin credentials.

Step 2: Navigate to Resources
In the left-hand menu, click Resources.
Under Resources, select Rooms & Equipment (or similar option depending on your version).

Step 3: Select the Meeting Room
Find the meeting room you want to check (e.g., LSP Admin Building – Meeting Room 206).
Click on the room name to open its settings.

Step 4: Check Booking Settings
In the Manage booking settings panel: 
Look for Booking window (days).
This value determines how far in advance meetings can be scheduled.
Example: If set to 730 days, meetings can only be scheduled up to 2 years in advance.

column31:
Symptoms
Screen edges darken → eventually black screen
BSOD with Stop Code: EXCEPTION_ON_INVALID_STACK
Issue recurs after restart


Step 1: Identify Problem Type
Hardware Indicators
Dark edges → LCD backlight degradation or eDP cable issue
Heat-related distortion possible due to thin design
Software Indicators
BSOD with invalid stack → driver/kernel conflict
Occurs during display failure → graphics driver likely involved

Step 2: Immediate Action
Do NOT replace hardware yet.
Focus on software updates first: 
Complete Windows Update (Windows 11 24H2)
Install Intel Graphics Driver 32.0.101.7026
Install Lenovo Power Management Driver 1.69.70.0

Critical Updates and Direct Impact
1. Intel Graphics Driver (32.0.101.7026)
Fixes black screen, flickering, and BSOD caused by GPU crashes
Improves memory stack handling → directly addresses EXCEPTION_ON_INVALID_STACK
Main Effect: Stabilizes GPU communication with LCD panel
2. Lenovo Power Management (1.69.70.0)
Controls power delivery to CPU, GPU, and LCD
Prevents stack corruption during sleep/wake cycles
Main Effect: Ensures stable voltage and timing for display components
3. Windows 11 Version 24H2
Kernel-level fixes for memory management and BSOD prevention
Improves driver compatibility and error handling
Main Effect: Patches OS to handle invalid stack exceptions gracefully
4. Intel Software Components
Support modules for Intel graphics and chipset
Optimize communication between GPU, CPU, and OS
Main Effect: Prevent cascading failures when display driver encounters errors
5. Intel Extension
Adds extended functionality for Intel graphics
Improves stability during high-load operations
Main Effect: Enhances overall graphics performance
6. MediaTek Net & Bluetooth Drivers
Network-related, not directly linked to display issue
Main Effect: Improves overall system stability during updates

Step 3: Update Logic
Intel Driver: Fixes black screen & graphics instability
Lenovo Power Management: Prevents invalid stack errors during power state changes
Windows 11 24H2: Kernel patches for BSOD & memory handling

Step 4: Execution
Plug in charger → ensure stable power
Let all updates download & install 100%
Click Restart Now when prompted
Allow multiple reboots if required

column2: [LSP Laptop] - My LSP laptop can not turn on after I locked screen
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
1. Problem Description The system experienced "Black Screen" freezes when entering or exiting sleep mode (Modern Standby). Users were unable to wake the device, necessitating a hard manual reset. Event logs confirmed an "Unexpected Shutdown" (Event 6008) preceded by a "Hardware Abstraction Layer" error (Event 21) regarding ACPI failure.

2. Root Cause Analysis
Driver-Firmware Mismatch: Multiple critical updates (Dell Firmware 0.1.17.0 and Intel System Drivers) were downloaded but not yet installed.

ACPI Protocol Conflict: The operating system was attempting to use updated power-state instructions on outdated firmware, causing a "Deadlock" where the Hardware Real-Time Clock became unreachable.
Pending State Instability: The system was in a hybrid state where core files were replaced on disk but the old versions were still active in RAM.
3. Solution Implemented
Full Update Cycle: Executed all pending Windows Updates, specifically prioritizing Intel Chipset and Dell Firmware components.
System Synchronization (Restart): Performed a full system reboot to allow the BIOS/UEFI to flash the new firmware and the Kernel to initialize the latest drivers.
ACPI Reset: The restart cleared the hardware registers and re-established the communication bridge between the OS and the motherboard.
4. Why This Works The restart phase is the only time the system can safely update the low-level code (Firmware) that controls electricity flow to components. By finishing the updates, the software (Windows) and hardware (Dell Mainboard) are now perfectly synchronized, allowing the ACPI methods to execute without errors when the screen turns off.

column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Resolution (Point‑to‑Point – Easy to Understand)
1. Issue Summary
User Sittharl was unable to connect to LSPConnect Wi‑Fi.
Cisco ISE logs showed that authentication was successful, but authorization was denied.
Endpoint MAC address: 14:75:5B:A7:31:09

2. Root Cause
The endpoint did not match any authorization rule that allows network access.
The 802.1X session fell back to the Default Authorization Rule.
The default rule applied the Authorization Profile: DenyAccess.
As a result, Cisco ISE returned a RADIUS Access‑Reject.
This issue was not related to the password or Active Directory authentication.
3. Action Taken by LV2: added the endpoint MAC address to the whitelist in Cisco ISE.MAC Address: 14:75:5B:A7:31:09
4. Result
The endpoint successfully reconnected to LSPConnect Wi‑Fi.
No further Access‑Reject events were observed.
The user is now able to access the network normally.

column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
This issue was resolved by deleting the folder:OneDrive\Apps\Microsoft Edge\Edge Workspaces 
Removing this folder cleared the corrupted Workspace data stored in OneDrive, which had been blocking synchronization.
The root cause is likely an account sync problem where Edge Workspaces data stored in OneDrive becomes corrupted or stuck, especially after account migrations or when multiple accounts are used. When the Workspace data inside:
OneDrive\Apps\Microsoft Edge\Edge Workspaces
is corrupted, Microsoft Edge cannot sync properly through OneDrive, resulting in Workspaces failing to load.
The Workspaces feature in Microsoft Edge does not work with my account - Microsoft Q&A

Additionally, Microsoft has acknowledged that the current sync issues with Edge Workspaces stored in OneDrive are due to the outdated Workspace architecture.
Microsoft is now migrating Workspaces off OneDrive/SharePoint and moving them to a dedicated Edge Sync service to prevent such issues.
Workspaces in Edge: Upcoming migration to improved architecture - M365 Admin
